title: 2013 HMMT February Algebra Problem 5
statement: Let \(a\) and \(b\) be real numbers, and let \(r, s\), and \(t\) be the roots of \(f(x)=x^{3}+a x^{2}+b x-1\). Also, \(g(x)=x^{3}+m x^{2}+n x+p\) has roots \(r^{2}, s^{2}\), and \(t^{2}\). If \(g(-1)=-5\), find the maximum possible value of \(b\).

solutions.text: \(\sqrt[{1+\sqrt{5}}]{ }\) By Vieta's Formulae, \(m=-\left(r^{2}+s^{2}+t^{2}\right)=-a^{2}+2 b, n=r^{2} s^{2}+s^{2} t^{2}+t^{2} r^{2}=\) \(b^{2}+2 a\), and \(p=-1\). Therefore, \(g(-1)=-1-a^{2}+2 b-b^{2}-2 a-1=-5 \Leftrightarrow(a+1)^{2}+(b-1)^{2}=5\). This is an equation of a circle, so \(b\) reaches its maximum when \(a+1=0 \Rightarrow a=-1\). When \(a=-1\), \(b=1 \pm \sqrt{5}\), so the maximum is \(1+\sqrt{5}\).
